Chapter 23 · Topic 4

CO

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentAir PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Carbon monoxide (incomplete combustion: vehicles, smoking, faulty heaters - colourless, odourless killer) binds haemoglobin 250x tighter than oxygen (carboxyhaemoglobin starving tissues), causing headache, dizziness, death silently. Catalytic converters oxidise CO to CO2; detectors alarm homes; ventilation prevents buildup. Smokers self-dose chronically (foetal risks in pregnancy). Silent affinity makes CO the stealth pollutant.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Odourless CO binds haemoglobin 250x tighter than O2.
  • Converters oxidise CO to CO2 in exhausts.
Remember
  • Silent, colourless, odourless - detectors save lives.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

CO poisoning works by forming

Solution: Ultra-tight binding starves tissues of oxygen silently.

Fig: Odourless carbon monoxide outcompetes oxygen 250 to one.

Chapter 23 · Topic 5

Smog

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentAir PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Smog splits classical (London coal-smoke plus fog - sulphurous, winter mornings) versus photochemical (Los Angeles NOx-VOC sunlight - ozonic, summer afternoons, eye-burning). Delhi mixes both seasonally (winter stubble-inversion classical, summer photochemical). Health tolls (asthma attacks, heart events spike) trigger emergency grades (school closures, construction halts). Source cuts (fuels, burning, dust) beat emergency responses structurally.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Coal-smoke winter versus photochemical summer smogs.
  • Delhi mixes both seasonally.
Smog types
PointDetail
Classical (London)Coal smoke + fog, sulphurous
Photochemical (LA)NOx+VOC+sun, ozonic
DelhiSeasonal mix of both

Chapter 23 · Topic 6

Acid rain

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentAir PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Acid rain (SO2 plus NOx oxidised to sulphuric-nitric acids, pH below 5.6) damages marble (Taj yellowing), forests (leaf leaching), crops, lakes (fish kills below pH 5) and metals (corrosion) - transported hundreds of kilometres downwind (Scandinavian lakes from British-German emissions). Tall-stack dispersal merely exports damage; scrubbers plus clean fuels prevent it. Liming lakes neutralises temporarily; emission cuts cure permanently.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Sulphuric-nitric precipitation below pH 5.6.
  • Marble, forests, lakes, metals all corrode.
Remember
  • Tall stacks export acid rain across borders.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Acid rain pH is below

Solution: Clean rain is mildly acidic (~5.6); acid rain falls below.

Chapter 23 · Topic 7

Sewage

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWater PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Sewage (domestic wastewater: organics, pathogens, nutrients, detergents) depletes oxygen (BOD overload killing fish), spreads waterborne diseases (cholera, typhoid, hepatitis), eutrophies waters (nutrient blooms), and stinks neighbourhoods. Treatment (primary settling, secondary biological flocs cutting BOD, tertiary disinfection) plus sewer networks plus Ganga-Yamuna action plans manage it. Open defecation-free (ODF) India cut direct loading massively.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Organic-pathogen-nutrient load depleting oxygen, spreading disease.
  • Treatment plus sewers plus river plans manage it.
Remember
  • BOD overload suffocates fish; pathogens sicken people.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Solution: Microbial decay consumes dissolved oxygen massively.

Industrial waste

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWater PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Industrial waste (chemical effluents: heavy metals, solvents, acids; thermal hot water; Minamata mercury, Bhopal gas tragedies warn) poisons waters, soils and air - common effluent treatment plants (CETPs) cluster-treat small units; zero-liquid-discharge (recycle all water) leads best practice; polluter-pays plus liability laws deter. Green chemistry (benign processes) prevents at source - treatment manages, prevention cures.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Chemical-thermal effluents poisoning water-soil-air.
  • CETPs cluster-treat; zero-discharge recycles all.
Remember
  • Minamata (mercury) and Bhopal warn industrial negligence.

Solution: Shared treatment makes small-unit compliance affordable.

Chapter 23 · Topic 9

BOD

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWater PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

BOD (biochemical oxygen demand: mg O2 microbes consume digesting organics in 5 days at 20C) measures pollution load - clean rivers below 5, sewage hundreds; falling BOD across treatment proves cleaning. DO (dissolved oxygen present) versus BOD (oxygen debt owed) confuse students; COD (chemical oxidation, faster, higher) complements. Ganga BOD monitoring tracks Namami Gange progress reach by reach.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Microbial oxygen debt measuring organic pollution.
  • Falling BOD proves treatment works.
Oxygen trio
PointDetail
DOOxygen present (fish need 5+ mg/L)
BODMicrobial oxygen demand (pollution load)
CODChemical oxidation demand (faster, higher)

Solution: Consumed organics leave microbes nothing to demand oxygen for.

Chapter 23 · Topic 10

Eutrophication

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWater PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Eutrophication (nutrient enrichment: sewage, fertiliser runoff feeding algal blooms that die, decay consuming oxygen - fish kills, stinking mats, biodiversity crash) ages lakes prematurely (natural succession accelerated hundred-fold). Phosphorus usually limits freshwater blooms (detergent bans help); nitrogen limits marine (dead zones: Gulf of Mexico). Sewage treatment plus buffer strips plus precision fertilisation starve blooms at source.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Nutrient blooms dying-decaying-suffocating waters.
  • Phosphorus limits freshwaters; nitrogen limits seas.
Remember
  • Dead zones (Gulf of Mexico) are eutrophication endpoints.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Eutrophication is primarily driven by excess nutrients mainly

Solution: Fertiliser plus sewage nutrients overfeed algae catastrophically.

Water-borne diseases

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWater PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Water-borne diseases (cholera Vibrio, typhoid Salmonella, hepatitis A/E, polio, giardiasis, amoebiasis - faecal-oral via contaminated water) sicken millions where sanitation fails; ORS plus antibiotics treat, vaccines (cholera, typhoid, polio, hepatitis) prevent, chlorination plus boiling plus filtration secure water. Swachh Bharat toilets plus piped treated water cut transmission structurally - sanitation is water-borne disease vaccine.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Faecal-oral pathogens via unsafe water sicken millions.
  • Treat (ORS, drugs), prevent (vaccines), secure (treat water).
Remember
  • Chlorination, boiling, filtration triple-secure drinking water.

1

Solution: Vibrio-contaminated water infects intestines massively.

Chapter 23 · Topic 12

Pesticides

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentSoil PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Pesticides (DDT, endosulfan, organophosphates - pest killers persisting in soils) biomagnify up food chains (DDT thinned eagle eggshells nearly extincting raptors), poison applicators (endosulfan Kasaragod tragedy), kill non-targets (bees collapsing), and breed resistance (pesticide treadmill). IPM (resistant varieties, biocontrol, need-based sprays), biopesticides (neem, Bt) and bans (DDT agriculture) reduce dependence - spray last, not first.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Persist, magnify, poison non-targets, breed resistance.
  • IPM plus biopesticides replace calendar spraying.
Remember
  • DDT eggshell thinning nearly erased raptors.
NEET Practice MCQ

Solution: DDT metabolite DDE thins shells crushing clutches.

Industrial chemicals (solvents, acids, PCBs, dioxins - persistent, toxic, bioaccumulative) leak from factories, e-waste and dumps into soil-water-food webs - Seveso dioxin (chloracne, cancers), Love Canal solvents (birth defects), e-waste Guiyu metals poisoning children. Green chemistry (benign synthesis), effluent treatment, e-waste rules and remediation (bioremediation microbes, phytoremediation plants) contain damage - prevent at design, treat at pipe, clean legacy sites.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Persistent toxic leaks poisoning soil-water-food webs.
  • Green chemistry prevents; treatment contains; remediation cleans.
Remember
  • Seveso and Love Canal warn chemical negligence.

Heavy metals

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentSoil PollutionStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic - non-degradable, biomagnifying) poison via water-food: Minamata mercury (fish to neurological disaster), itai-itai cadmium (rice to bone pain), arsenic groundwater (Bengal-Bangladesh skin lesions-cancers), lead (paint-petrol child brain damage). Chelation therapy plus clean water plus phytoremediation (hyperaccumulators mining soils) respond. Non-degradable means dilute-or-bury dilemmas persist centuries.

  • Non-degradable metals biomagnifying to neurological-bone damage.
  • Minamata (Hg), itai-itai (Cd), Bengal arsenic warn.

Chapter 23 · Topic 15

Biomagnification

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentBiological EffectsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Biomagnification (concentration rising per trophic level: water ppb to plankton ppm to fish ppm to eagles/f humans ppm - DDT, mercury, PCBs) happens because toxins store in fat, resist metabolism and pass upward with ~10 percent energy (biomass shrinks concentrating residues). Top predators and nursing infants (breast-milk fat) face highest doses. DDT eagle crashes plus Minamata cats dancing proved invisible concentration visibly.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Fat-stored persistent toxins concentrate upward per level.
  • Top predators and infants face peak doses.
Fig: ppb in water becomes ppm in predators - fat-stored toxins concentrate upward.

Chapter 23 · Topic 16

Bioaccumulation

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentBiological EffectsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Bioaccumulation (buildup within one organism over lifetime: mercury in tuna muscle, lead in bones, DDT in adipose) differs from biomagnification (rise across levels) - accumulation feeds magnification upward. Long-lived predators accumulate most (old tuna, eagles); excretion pathways (milk, eggs, hair) offload partially (nursing transfers to infants - benefit-risk balances). Monitoring tissues (hair mercury, fat DDT) tracks exposure histories.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Within-organism buildup over lifetime (vs across-level magnification).
  • Old predators accumulate most; milk/eggs offload partially.
Remember
  • Accumulation (individual) feeds magnification (food chain).
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Bioaccumulation differs from biomagnification as buildup

Solution: Individual loading precedes food-chain concentration.

Chapter 23 · Topic 17

Greenhouse effect

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentGlobal Environmental ProblemsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Greenhouse effect (atmospheric gases - water vapour, CO2, methane, N2O, ozone - transparent to incoming shortwave, absorbing outgoing longwave) warms Earth 33C above freezing (natural blanket enabling life); enhanced effect (fossil CO2, methane leaks, N2O fertilisers) thickens blanket overheating. Venus (runaway) versus Mars (thin, frozen) bracket outcomes. Tyndall measured gas absorption; Arrhenius predicted fossil warming in 1896 - physics known for a century.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Gases pass sunlight in, trap heat out - natural blanket plus human thickening.
  • 33C natural warming enables life; excess overheats.
Remember
  • Venus runaway versus Mars frozen bracket greenhouse fates.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Natural greenhouse effect warms Earth by about

Solution: Gas blanket keeps average 15C instead of -18C.

Fig: Sunlight enters freely; greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat - blanket physics.

Chapter 23 · Topic 18

Global warming

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentGlobal Environmental ProblemsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Global warming (enhanced greenhouse from fossil CO2, methane, N2O plus deforestation) raises temperatures (~1.2C so far), melts ice (sea-level rise threatening coasts/islands), intensifies extremes (heatwaves, floods, droughts, cyclones), shifts species poleward/upward, acidifies oceans (CO2 dissolving). Paris Agreement (well below 2C, pursue 1.5C) plus net-zero pledges plus renewables bend curves; adaptation (seawalls, heat plans, resilient crops) manages committed change.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Fossil-driven heating melting ice, intensifying extremes, shifting species.
  • Mitigation (cut emissions) plus adaptation (manage change).

OceansAcidification (CO2 dissolving)

Chapter 23 · Topic 19

Ozone depletion

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentGlobal Environmental ProblemsStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Ozone depletion (CFCs, halons releasing chlorine/bromine catalytically destroying stratospheric O3 - one atom kills 100,000 molecules) thinned Antarctic ozone hole each spring (UV-B floods raising skin cancer, cataracts, crop damage, plankton kills). Montreal Protocol (1987, universal ratification) phased CFCs - healing spots now appearing, policy triumph proving cooperation works. Ozone (stratospheric shield) versus smog-ozone (ground pollutant) differ by altitude - good up high, bad down low.
NEET Snapshot:
  • CFC chlorine catalytically destroys stratospheric shield.
  • Montreal Protocol phases CFCs; healing begins.
Remember
  • Stratospheric ozone shields; ground ozone chokes - altitude decides.

1

Solution: Universal CFC phase-out lets ozone holes heal.

Topic in Depth

Acid rain (SO2/NOx to sulphuric-nitric acids below pH 5.6) corrodes marble (Taj), forests, lakes and metals hundreds of kilometres downwind - tall stacks merely export damage; scrubbers plus clean fuels prevent it. Liming lakes neutralises temporarily. (Cross-link to Air Pollution acid-rain topic - same chemistry, global-transport angle here.) Control at source (desulphurisation, catalysts, renewables) cures permanently.
NEET Snapshot:

  • Source cuts (not tall stacks) solve permanently.
Remember
  • See Air Pollution acid-rain topic for chemistry detail.

Chapter 23 · Topic 21

Solid waste

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWaste ManagementStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Solid waste (municipal garbage, construction debris, e-waste, biomedical sharps) buries land (landfills leaking leachate), burns air (open burning dioxins), and wastes resources (linear take-make-dispose). Segregation at source (wet-dry-hazardous) enables composting, recycling and safe disposal respectively; Swachh Bharat built toilets plus waste systems; EPR (producers take back packaging, e-waste) internalises costs. Reduce-reuse-recycle hierarchy orders responses.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Segregate wet-dry-hazardous; compost, recycle, dispose safely.
  • EPR makes producers own packaging afterlife.
Remember
  • Segregation at source enables all downstream handling.

Chapter 23 · Topic 22

Sewage treatment

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWaste ManagementStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Sewage treatment stages physics then biology: primary settling (grit, solids), secondary aeration tanks (microbial flocs cutting BOD - activated sludge recycled), tertiary disinfection (chlorine/UV) plus nutrient removal - effluent safe for rivers, sludge digested to biogas plus manure. Ganga-Yamuna action plans plus Namami Gange scale STPs; decentralised (septic, constructed wetlands) serve unsewered areas. BOD fall proves cleaning stage by stage.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Settle, biologically clean (flocs cut BOD), disinfect - staged cleaning.
  • Sludge digests to biogas plus manure.
Remember
  • BOD crash across aeration tanks proves treatment works.
NEET Practice MCQ
1

Activated sludge in sewage treatment contains

Solution: Aerated microbe masses consume sewage BOD biologically.

Fig: Settle solids, flocs cut BOD, disinfect effluent - staged cleaning.

Chapter 23 · Topic 23

Recycling

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWaste ManagementStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Recycling (paper, glass, metals, plastics sorted and reprocessed) saves energy (aluminium 95 percent), trees, ores and landfill space - informal kabadiwala networks recycle efficiently (India recycles PET highly); e-waste rules channel circuit boards to authorised dismantlers (precious-metal recovery); plastic roads (shredded bitumen mix) pave waste into highways. Segregation quality decides recycling economics - mixed waste downgrades to downcycling.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Reprocess discards into inputs saving energy-materials-landfill.
  • Kabadiwala networks plus e-waste rules organise Indian recycling.
Remember
  • Aluminium recycling saves 95 percent smelting energy.

Chapter 23 · Topic 24

Composting

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWaste ManagementStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Composting (aerobic microbial decay of wet waste into humus: pit, windrow, vermi-worm, in-vessel methods) returns nutrients to soils, cuts methane (versus landfilling organics), and suppresses landfill burden - browns (carbon dry leaves) plus greens (nitrogen kitchen waste) plus air plus moisture recipe success. Vermicompost (earthworm premium) fetches prices; municipal compost greens cities. Segregated wet waste composts; mixed waste contaminates.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Aerobic decay turning wet waste to humus.
  • Browns plus greens plus air plus moisture recipe.
Remember
  • Vermicompost worms upgrade waste to premium manure.

Chapter 23 · Topic 25

Biodegradable waste

Environmental IssuesEcology and EnvironmentWaste ManagementStep-by-step Topic

Topic in Depth

Biodegradable waste (food scraps, paper, garden trimmings, cow dung - microbially decomposable in weeks-months) composts, biogases and mulches back into cycles - segregation keeps it clean for processing. Oxo-degradable plastics fragment (not biodegrade - microplastic caution); truly compostable bags (EN-certified) digest fully. Time-bound decay defines biodegradability - months, not centuries.
NEET Snapshot:
  • Microbe-degradable in weeks-months back into cycles.
  • Compost, biogas and mulch absorb biodegradables.
Remember
  • Oxo-fragmenting plastics are not truly biodegradable.

Plastic Waste Rules (extended producer responsibility, carry-bag thickness norms) plus Swachhata drives manage nationally. Persistence demands prevention over cure.
